advances: The complete permitted primitive-element family at p=5 has an all-ten-sink comparison certificate. Together with accepted fact ee2c0378f6772485, this establishes the parent harmonic comparison and its collision-or-five-generated-lattice-points consequence for every prime p>=5. The p=5 part uses a complete exact finite-field reduction and explicitly checked rational bounds. The graph normalization, uniqueness, reduction, and geometric consumer are proved analytically. This excludes the proposed simultaneous distinct-label and reflection-at-most-three realization throughout this prime-cycle family; it does not settle the locked weak Oertel conjecture.

proof:
First, the field expression is well defined for every primitive element in the stated range. Put \(q=2^{p-1}\) and \(K=\mathbb F_q\subset\mathbb F_{q^2}\). Since \(p\mid q-1\), the element \(\omega\) belongs to \(K\). If \(\gamma=1+\alpha+\omega/\alpha\) belonged to \(K\), then \(\alpha\notin K\) would have monic quadratic minimal polynomial \(x^2+(1+\gamma)x+\omega\) over \(K\). Its norm would be \(\omega\), of order \(p\). Its actual norm \(\alpha^{q+1}\) has order \(q-1>p\), a contradiction. Thus \(\gamma\ne0\). For \(p\ge7\), accepted fact ee2c0378f6772485 applies with the identical \(n,Q,m,\alpha,\omega,c,X_{i,t},U_i,V_i,Z_i,A_j,B_j\) and the identical deletion rule. It supplies the required harmonic comparison, including its assertion for arbitrary \(c\). It remains to establish the new \(p=5\) case and the common consumer.

Fix \(p=5\), hence \(Q=255\) and \(m=51\). For now \(c\) may be any shift. All indices in the graph calculations are modulo 255. The retained equations in the canonical aliases are exactly

\[
\begin{aligned}
2U_i&=V_i+Z_{i-1},&
2V_i&=U_{i-m}+Z_{i-m}
&& (i\not\equiv0\pmod m),\\
2Z_{i+c}&=U_i+V_{i+1}
&&&& (i\not\equiv0,-1\pmod m).
\end{aligned}
\]

Indeed, precisely \(U_{jm},V_{jm}\) are deleted. A type-zero or type-one equation at a retained center has no deleted parent. A type-two equation at \(Z_{i+c}\) has a deleted parent exactly when \(i\equiv0,-1\pmod m\). Its retained center is then one of the ten stated sinks. There are 755 retained labels and 745 retained equations, respectively 250, 250, and 245 of the three types.

The full directed graph, with each edge from a center to a parent, is strongly connected. The closed type paths \(0\to1\to0\), \(0\to2\to0\), and \(0\to1\to2\to0\) give exponent increments \(-m\), \(-(1+c)\), and \(-(m+c)\). The subgroup they generate contains \(m\) and \(m-1\), hence one. In a finite cyclic group, the nonnegative semigroup generated by increments is their subgroup, since each inverse is a nonnegative multiple. Thus every type-zero label reaches every other type-zero label, and the direct type edges give strong connectivity for all types.

Every retained nonsink reaches a sink through retained equations. Follow an original path to a deleted label, and stop at its first retained center whose equation was lost. Such a center occurs before the first deleted label and is a sink by the classification above. All earlier edges are retained. Consequently the scalar homogeneous problem with zero boundary has no positive maximum or negative minimum: an extremum would propagate along a retained path to a zero sink. The square integer system on the 745 nonsinks is therefore invertible over \(\mathbb Q\). The maximum principle gives nonnegative unit-boundary solutions, and uniqueness applied to their sum shows that each harmonic coefficient vector sums to one. This also justifies the absorption interpretation: finiteness and the paths to sinks give a common positive probability of absorption within a fixed number of steps, and iteration makes survival probability tend to zero. Positivity at every individual sink for the selected parents will follow from the strict rational bounds below; it is not inferred from strong connectivity after deletion.

Here is the exact reduction used for those bounds. Put \(D=4^5-1=1023\). Combining the first two retained equations and iterating around a retained cycle gives

\[
DU_i=\sum_{k=0}^4 4^{4-k}
\bigl(Z_{i-(k+1)m}+2Z_{i-1-km}\bigr)
\qquad(i\not\equiv0\pmod m).
\]

The two cycle identities are \(4U_i-U_{i-m}=Z_{i-m}+2Z_{i-1}\) and \(4V_i-V_{i-m}=Z_{i-m-1}+2Z_{i-m}\). Applying them to the type-two equation gives

\(4Z_{i+c}-Z_{i+c-m}=Z_{i-1}+Z_{i-m}+Z_{i+1-m}\).

Iteration five times therefore gives the positive reduced system

\[
DZ_{i+c}=\sum_{k=0}^4 4^{4-k}
\bigl(Z_{i-1-km}+Z_{i-(k+1)m}+Z_{i+1-(k+1)m}\bigr)
\qquad(i\not\equiv0,-1\pmod m).
\]

These reductions are equivalent to the original harmonic problem, with the same ten independent sink values. To see sufficiency, reconstruct \(U_i\) from its cycle formula and set \(V_i=2U_i-Z_{i-1}\). The type-zero and type-one equations follow. On each retained type-two residue cycle put \(E_i=2Z_{i+c}-U_i-V_{i+1}\). The reduced equation, or its equivalent one-step form, gives \(4E_i-E_{i-m}=0\). Iterating around that cycle yields \(DE_i=0\), hence the original type-two equation. For equivalence of each iterated relation with its one-step relation, define \((Tg)_i=g_{i-m}\) on that cycle. Then \(T^5=I\), and \(4I-T\) has inverse \(D^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^4 4^{4-k}T^k\). Thus the reduced integer matrix with its ten boundary rows is invertible over \(\mathbb Q\). The certificate below also checks reconstruction against every original retained equation independently of this equivalence argument.

We next give the complete primitive-element reduction. Work in the quotient by \(f(x)=x^8+x^4+x^3+x^2+1\) over \(\mathbb F_2\), and let \(a\) be the class of \(x\). Polynomial division gives

\[
\begin{aligned}
a^{255}&=1,&a^{85}&=a^7+a^6+a^4+a^2+a,\\
a^{51}&=a^3+a,&a^{15}&=a^5+a^2+a.
\end{aligned}
\]

The last three values differ from one. Since \(255=3\cdot5\cdot17\), the first identity and these three tests prove that \(a\) has order 255. Its distinct nonzero powers exhaust the 255 nonzero elements of the quotient, making it a field. In particular, \(f\) is irreducible, and every primitive element of this field is \(a^e\) with \(\gcd(e,255)=1\).

For a polynomial residue \(\sum_{j=0}^7 b_j a^j\), its integer encoding in the next table is \(\sum_{j=0}^7 b_j2^j\). The table checks the identity \(1+a^e+a^{50e}=a^{ec}\) by giving its common encoded value. The displayed representatives \(e\) have disjoint orbits \(\{2^je\pmod{255}:0\le j<8\}\), each of size eight. Their union is all 128 units modulo 255. These finite set equalities are checked in the certificate. Squaring the field identity preserves \(c\), so it holds with the same shift throughout each orbit. Every primitive element is therefore covered. Conversely, each row supplies a primitive element realizing its listed shift.

The last three columns concern the harmonic measures for that shift. At the listed retained index \(i\), every coefficient of both \(\mu_{V_i}\) and \(\mu_{Z_{i-1}}\), in the sink order \(A_0,\ldots,A_4,B_0,\ldots,B_4\), is strictly between the lower and upper numerators divided by 100000.

|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 26 | 6 | 24 | 6919 | 12930 |
| 7 | 169 | 99 | 18 | 9330 | 10706 |
| 11 | 92 | 131 | 39 | 8886 | 10735 |

| 19 | 40 | 108 | 32 | 9521 | 10548 |
| 23 | 140 | 230 | 28 | 8424 | 11368 |
| 29 | 39 | 206 | 50 | 9259 | 10797 |
| 31 | 231 | 117 | 50 | 9408 | 10596 |
| 37 | 213 | 245 | 50 | 9509 | 10499 |
| 43 | 115 | 17 | 49 | 8327 | 11025 |
| 47 | 156 | 130 | 1 | 9880 | 10121 |
| 53 | 177 | 56 | 26 | 9408 | 10594 |
| 59 | 253 | 158 | 2 | 7985 | 12024 |
| 61 | 88 | 135 | 13 | 9558 | 10453 |

Each lower numerator exceeds \(100000/15\), and each upper numerator is less than \(200000/15\). These bounds prove the stronger p=5 assertion, including strict positivity at all ten individual sinks. In particular, each ratio between the two parents at a fixed sink is less than two, hence less than three.

The following self-contained certificate checks the entire table by exact arithmetic. Finite-field multiplication is explicit binary polynomial multiplication modulo \(f\). The 255-by-255 matrix is the reduced system just derived, with ten independent unit-boundary columns. The certificate solves it over \(\mathbb Q\), checks the exact matrix residual, reconstructs all 755 coefficient vectors, and checks all 745 original midpoint equations, all ten boundary vectors, nonnegativity, unit sums, and the twenty strict bounds for each of the 16 shifts. The original rows are generated directly from \(X_{i,t}\) and the deletion rule. Thus the checked residuals and the analytic uniqueness argument identify the rational solution being bounded. There are no floating-point or randomized decisions. This code was run with SageMath 10.8 using `sage --nodotsage --python -`, with exit status zero.

```python
from math import gcd
from sage.all import ZZ, QQ, matrix, vector

table = [
    (1,26,6,24,6919,12930), (7,169,99,18,9330,10706),
    (11,92,131,39,8886,10735), (13,157,2,2,9765,10224),
    (19,40,108,32,9521,10548), (23,140,230,28,8424,11368),
    (29,39,206,50,9259,10797), (31,231,117,50,9408,10596),
    (37,213,245,50,9509,10499), (43,115,17,49,8327,11025),
    (47,156,130,1,9880,10121), (53,177,56,26,9408,10594),
    (59,253,158,2,7985,12024), (61,88,135,13,9558,10453),
    (91,10,77,23,8775,11060), (127,202,57,1,7999,12002)]

def mul(u, v):
    result = 0
    while v:
        if v & 1:
            result ^= u
        v >>= 1
        u <<= 1
        if u & 256:
            u ^= 285
    return result

def power(u, exponent):
    result = 1
    while exponent:
        if exponent & 1:
            result = mul(result, u)
        u = mul(u, u)
        exponent >>= 1
    return result

assert [power(2,e) for e in (255,85,51,15)] == [1,214,10,38]
units = {e for e in range(1,255) if gcd(e,255) == 1}
seen = set()
for e,c,encoded,i,lower,upper in table:
    orbit = {(e*2**j)%255 for j in range(8)}
    assert len(orbit) == 8 and orbit <= units and not (orbit & seen)
    seen |= orbit
    b = power(2,e)
    assert 1 ^ b ^ power(b,50) == encoded == power(b,c)
    assert encoded != 0
    for exponent in orbit:
        b = power(2,exponent)
        assert 1 ^ b ^ power(b,50) == power(b,c)
assert seen == units and len(units) == 128
assert sorted(c for e,c,encoded,i,lower,upper in table) == [
    10,26,39,40,88,92,115,140,156,157,169,177,202,213,231,253]

Q, m, D = 255, 51, 1023
deleted = {(j*m,0) for j in range(5)} | {
    ((j*m-1)%Q,1) for j in range(5)}
labels = [(i,t) for i in range(Q) for t in range(3)
          if (i,t) not in deleted]
for e,c,encoded,witness,lower,upper in table:
    parents = {(i,t): [((i-[1,m-1,c][t])%Q,s)
                      for s in range(3) if s != t]
               for i in range(Q) for t in range(3)}
    rows = [(z,parents[z]) for z in labels
            if all(parent not in deleted for parent in parents[z])]
    sinks = [((c-1+j*m)%Q,2) for j in range(5)] + [
        ((c+j*m)%Q,2) for j in range(5)]
    assert len(labels) == 755 and len(rows) == 745
    assert [sum(z[1] == t for z,ps in rows) for t in range(3)] == [250,250,245]
    assert set(labels)-{z for z,ps in rows} == set(sinks)
    reached = set(sinks)
    while True:
        enlarged = reached | {z for z,ps in rows if any(p in reached for p in ps)}
        if enlarged == reached:
            break
        reached = enlarged
    assert reached == set(labels)

    M = matrix(ZZ,Q,Q)
    boundary = matrix(ZZ,Q,10)
    for i in range(Q):
        if i%m in (0,m-1):
            continue
        r = (i+c)%Q
        M[r,r] += D
        for k in range(5):
            for h in (i-1-k*m, i-(k+1)*m, i+1-(k+1)*m):
                M[r,h%Q] -= 4**(4-k)
    for h,(s,t) in enumerate(sinks):
        assert not any(M.row(s))
        M[s,s] = 1
        boundary[s,h] = 1
    Z = M.change_ring(QQ).solve_right(boundary)
    assert M*Z == boundary
    U = {i: sum((4**(4-k)*(Z.row((i-(k+1)*m)%Q)
                            +2*Z.row((i-1-k*m)%Q)) for k in range(5)),
                vector(QQ,10))/D for i in range(Q) if i%m != 0}
    measure = {(i,2): Z.row(i) for i in range(Q)}
    measure.update({(i,0): u for i,u in U.items()})
    measure.update({((i-1)%Q,1): 2*u-Z.row((i-1)%Q)
                    for i,u in U.items()})
    assert set(measure) == set(labels)
    for z,ps in rows:
        assert 2*measure[z] == measure[ps[0]]+measure[ps[1]]
    for h,s in enumerate(sinks):
        assert measure[s] == vector(QQ,[int(j == h) for j in range(10)])
    assert all(min(u) >= 0 and sum(u) == 1 for u in measure.values())

    assert 1 <= witness < m
    center = (witness,0)
    assert center in {z for z,ps in rows}
    assert parents[center] == [((witness-1)%Q,1),((witness-1)%Q,2)]
    u,v = [measure[parent] for parent in parents[center]]
    assert all(QQ(lower)/100000 < value < QQ(upper)/100000
               for value in list(u)+list(v))
    assert 15*lower > 100000 and 15*upper < 200000
    assert all(QQ(1)/15 < value < QQ(2)/15 for value in list(u)+list(v))
    assert min(list(3*u-v)+list(3*v-u)) > QQ(1)/15
print('128 primitive elements in 16 Frobenius classes verified')
print('16 graphs: each 755 labels, 745 original equations, 10 unit-vector sinks verified')
print('all 320 selected parent coefficients lie strictly between 1/15 and 2/15')
```

Finally, use the factor-three comparison, proved above at p=5 and supplied by the declared predecessor for p>=7. Assign arbitrary rational sink positions in \(\mathbb Q^N\). Each realized label is their convex combination, and the sinks remain among the labels, so their hull equals \(P\). All positions are rational. A common denominator puts \(\mathcal L\) inside a dilation of \(\mathbb Z^N\), which makes \(B\) finite.

For the selected row, the two points \((3V_i-Z_{i-1})/2\) and \((3Z_{i-1}-V_i)/2\) have strictly positive coefficients at all sinks, and those coefficients sum to one. Thus both points belong to \(P\). They also equal \(2V_i-U_i\) and \(2Z_{i-1}-U_i\), respectively, so both belong to \(\mathcal L\). Put \(v=V_i-U_i\in\mathcal L\). The five points \(U_i+tv\), for \(t=-2,-1,0,1,2\), all belong to \(B\). If \(V_i=Z_{i-1}\), two retained labels collide. Otherwise \(v\ne0\), the five points are distinct, and their five oriented displacements give \(r_B^{\mathcal L}(U_i)\ge5\). This proves the consumer for every rational sink assignment, including assignments with affine dependencies or coincident sink positions.
statement:
Let \(p\ge5\) be prime, put \(n=2p-2\), \(Q=2^n-1\), and \(m=Q/p\), and let \(\alpha\) be any primitive element of \(\mathbb F_{2^n}\). Put \(\omega=\alpha^m\). The element \(1+\alpha+\omega/\alpha\) is nonzero, so define the unique \(c\in\mathbb Z/Q\mathbb Z\) by \(\alpha^c=1+\alpha+\omega/\alpha\).

Start with labels \(X_{i,t}\), where \(i\in\mathbb Z/Q\mathbb Z\) and \(t\in\{0,1,2\}\), and equations

\[
2X_{i,t}=X_{i-d_t,s}+X_{i-d_t,u},
\qquad (d_0,d_1,d_2)=(1,m-1,c),
\qquad \{s,u,t\}=\{0,1,2\}.
\]

Delete \(X_{jm,0}\) and \(X_{jm-1,1}\), for \(0\le j<p\), and every equation with a deleted endpoint. Use precisely the aliases of accepted fact ee2c0378f6772485: \(U_i=X_{i,0}\), \(V_i=X_{i-1,1}\), and \(Z_i=X_{i,2}\). The retained labels without equations are exactly \(A_j=Z_{c-1+jm}\) and \(B_j=Z_{c+jm}\), for \(0\le j<p\).

The harmonic boundary problem at these \(2p\) sinks has a unique solution. Let \(\mu_Y(s)\) be the coefficient of sink \(s\) at the retained label \(Y\), with the sinks prescribed as the independent standard basis vectors of \(\mathbb Q^{2p}\). Some retained equation \(2U_i=V_i+Z_{i-1}\), with \(i\not\equiv0\pmod m\), satisfies, at every individual sink \(s\),

\[
0<\mu_{V_i}(s)<3\mu_{Z_{i-1}}(s),
\qquad
0<\mu_{Z_{i-1}}(s)<3\mu_{V_i}(s).
\]

For \(p=5\), the set of permitted shifts is exactly

\(\{10,26,39,40,88,92,115,140,156,157,169,177,202,213,231,253\}\).

The table in the proof specifies an index \(i\) for each shift for which the stronger bounds \(1/15<\mu_{V_i}(s)<2/15\) and \(1/15<\mu_{Z_{i-1}}(s)<2/15\) hold at all ten sinks. For \(p\ge7\), the displayed factor-three conclusion holds for arbitrary \(c\) modulo \(Q\), by the accepted predecessor.

For every integer \(N\ge1\) and every assignment of positions in \(\mathbb Q^N\) to the \(2p\) sinks, realize all retained labels by their unique harmonic solution. Let \(P\) be the convex hull of the realized positions, let \(\mathcal L\) be their generated additive group, and put \(B=P\cap\mathcal L\). Define \(r_B^{\mathcal L}(y)=|\{v\in\mathcal L:y+v,y-v\in B\}|\), with oriented displacements and zero counted once. At the graph-dependent index just specified, either \(V_i=Z_{i-1}\), or \(B\) contains five distinct collinear points centered at \(U_i\) and \(r_B^{\mathcal L}(U_i)\ge5\).
